test.name: Spec 0010 spike: posix_spawn flags, fd map, argv, env, cwd

expected: posix_spawn with POSIX_SPAWN_SETSID, SETSIGDEF (all signals), an empty SETSIGMASK, CLOEXEC_DEFAULT and START_SUSPENDED, fd sources duplicated to 10 and up first, addopen /dev/null on 0, adddup2 to 1, 2, 3 and addchdir_np gives a child whose argv, env, cwd, signal state and fds 0 to 3 are exactly the plan's (spec 0010 AC-1, Adapter macOS row Spawn)
actual: Suspended child read from the kernel before it ran any code: PROC_PIDLISTFDS lists exactly fds 0,1,2,3 (all vnodes) although the parent had a leaked non-CLOEXEC fd; fd 0 is /dev/null, fds 1, 2, 3 match the stdout spool, stderr spool and instance.lock by dev and inode. KERN_PROCARGS2 argv equals [canonical executable, plan args] exactly, including a label with spaces, quotes, $( ), backticks, |, &, >, *, ~, ü and 空; env is exactly the two plan entries (the parent-only variable is absent). cwd (PROC_PIDVNODEPATHINFO) is the plan cwd. kinfo_proc: p_sigmask 0 although the parent blocked SIGUSR1; p_sigignore 0x18488000, which is only the kernel's default-ignore set (SIGURG, SIGCHLD, SIGIO, SIGWINCH, SIGINFO), so SIGPIPE and SIGHUP that the parent ignored are back to default; sigfillset in setsigdefault was accepted. After SIGCONT, argv-serve.json equals the plan args byte for byte and no pwned file exists anywhere under the test root. A daemon with fds 0, 1, 2 closed (lock, stdout and stderr spool landing on 0, 1, 2) still gives the child the right fds 0..3 when sources are first duplicated to 10 and up; the naive mapping without that step gives the child only fds 0 and 3, both /dev/null. posix_spawn returns ENOENT for a missing executable, EACCES for a non-executable file, and ENOENT for a missing cwd (addchdir_np), with no child in each case. Helper path: stdin pipe written then closed, the fake init helper read to EOF, exited 0, and token.sha256 equals the SHA-256 of the bytes written; it held the lock on fd 3 while it ran. For step 3: libc 0.2.190 has no POSIX_SPAWN_SETSID (0x0400 in sys/spawn.h), so the adapter declares it.
